method: Each scenario runs once in a separate process with its own freshly created database, document storage and master key, deleted afterwards. HELD: the control behaved as the catalogue states. FAILED: it did not. ERROR: the scenario could not complete.

results.title: Control: an untouched signed document
results.defence: Shows the lab is not rigged to report failures: an honest document must verify.
steps: Signed a fresh document
Verified it without any change

results.title: Substitute the stored document
results.defence: Verification recomputes SHA-256 from the stored bytes and compares it with the signed hash.
steps: Signed "Pay the supplier 1,000.00"
Replaced the stored bytes with validly encrypted "Pay the supplier 9,000.00"
Verified

results.title: Flip one bit of the encrypted blob
results.defence: The GCM authentication tag fails, which verification reports as tampering.
steps: Signed a document
Flipped the last bit of its ciphertext on disk
Verified

results.title: Corrupt the signature value
results.defence: Cryptographic verification under the certificate's public key.
steps: Signed a document
Flipped a bit in the stored signature
Verified

results.title: Replay a genuine signature onto another document
results.defence: The signature covers the document's own hash, so it does not verify for different content.
steps: Signed "Contract A" and "Contract B" with the same certificate
Copied A's signature and time-stamp onto B
Verified B

results.title: Relabel the signature algorithm
results.defence: The algorithm is identified from the certificate's key material, and providers refuse foreign keys.
steps: Signed under ECDSA_P256
Relabelled the signature and certificate records as RSA
Verified

results.title: Point the signature at another certificate
results.defence: Key-to-record consistency is checked before any cryptographic operation.
steps: Signed a document
Pointed the signature at a RSA certificate
Verified

results.title: Keep using a signature after key compromise
results.defence: Revocation is read from the CA-signed CRL under the timestamp-aware policy.
steps: Signed a document
Revoked the certificate for keyCompromise with no invalidity date (a new CRL is issued)
Verified

results.title: Swap in another signature's time-stamp
results.defence: The token's message imprint must equal SHA-256 of this signature value.
steps: Signed two documents
Attached the second signature's genuine time-stamp token to the first
Verified the first

results.title: Forge the revocation list
results.defence: A CRL is used only after its CA signature, issuer and freshness check; otherwise status is unavailable.
steps: Signed a document
Altered the newest CA-signed revocation list in the database
Verified

results.title: Verify an exported CMS signature against altered content
results.defence: The signed message-digest attribute covers the exact document bytes.
results.observed: CMS verification: original VALID, altered INVALID
steps: Signed "Deliver 500 units" (a detached CMS signature is produced too)
Verified the CMS signature against the original
Verified it against "Deliver 900 units"

evidence.explanation: The document differs from the document that was signed.

results.title: Steal a copy of a protected master key file
results.defence: The file holds the master key wrapped with AES-256-GCM under a scrypt-derived key (lib/crypto/key-custody.ts); without the passphrase it does not unwrap.
results.expected: Refused without the passphrase and with a guessed one; the right passphrase recovers the same key
results.observed: Without the passphrase: refused; with a guessed passphrase: refused; with the right passphrase: the same key, which decrypts the copied private key
steps: Signed a document, so an encrypted private key exists in the database
Wrapped the sandbox master key under a random passphrase (scrypt N=131072, r=8, p=1; AES-256-GCM) and copied the file
Tried to unwrap the copy with no passphrase
Tried a guessed passphrase
Unwrapped it with the right passphrase, as a control

evidence.withoutPassphrase: The master key is passphrase-protected; set OMNITRUST_MASTER_PASSPHRASE in the environment of the process that needs it
evidence.guessedPassphrase: The master key could not be unwrapped: the passphrase is wrong or the key file was altered
evidence.limitation: With the default plaintext key file the same copy decrypts every private key directly; this scenario tests the protected configuration, not the default.

results.title: Edit an audit log row
results.defence: The hash chain: each entry's hash covers its fields and its predecessor's hash.
results.expected: Integrity check fails at exactly that entry
steps: Produced audit entries by signing a document
Edited audit entry 4 directly in the database
Ran the integrity check

firstBreak.detail: entry 4 (DOCUMENT_UPLOADED) stores 6c7e5f970d92381f... but its contents hash to dcbd4b1b559e218b...: this entry was altered

results.title: Rewrite the audit log and recompute every hash
results.defence: A signed, time-stamped checkpoint committed to the original chain head.
results.expected: Chain check fooled, checkpoint check reports LOG_REWRITTEN
results.observed: Hash chain alone: fooled (verifies); with checkpoints: LOG_REWRITTEN
steps: Produced audit entries and created a signed checkpoint
Edited entry 4, then recomputed and rewrote every later hash
Ran the chain check, then the checkpoint reconciliation

results.title: Delete the newest audit entries
results.defence: A signed checkpoint covering those entries.
results.expected: Chain check fooled, checkpoint check reports LOG_TRUNCATED
results.observed: Hash chain alone: fooled (verifies); with checkpoints: LOG_TRUNCATED
steps: Produced audit entries and created a signed checkpoint
Deleted the newest 3 entries
Ran the chain check, then the checkpoint reconciliation

results.title: Brute-force a password
results.defence: Per-account failed-login throttling, applied before the password is checked.
results.expected: Locked out after 5 failures, even with the correct password
results.observed: Locked after 5 failures; the correct password is refused for 899 s
steps: Tried 5 wrong passwords before the account was locked
Then tried the correct password
The limiter is consulted first, as in the login route
